samples.summary: editor.ts's same-cell branch still resolves cell parentage through the body-only `layout.blockParentMap`, so the fix the diff applied to the cursor-only branch does not reach it
samples.evidence: The diff switched the cursor-only branch to `doc.blockParentMap` (editor.ts:1732) with an explicit comment that `layout.blockParentMap` is the *body* layout's map and returns `undefined` for a caret inside a header/footer table cell. The same-cell cross-block branch two hunks above is unchanged: `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1683-1684` still calls `layout.blockParentMap.get(range.anchor.blockId)` / `.get(range.focus.blockId)`. For a multi-block selection inside a *header/footer* table cell both lookups yield `undefined`, the branch is skipped, `doc.getBlockIndex()` returns -1 for cell blocks, and control falls through to the cursor-only fallback — so `indent()` / `outdent()` (and `applyBlockStyle` / `toggleList`, which share the walker) plan only the caret block's subtree instead of the whole selection. The equivalent walker in text-editor.ts uses the active-layout resolver (`packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2829`, via `getCellInfo` → `getActiveLayout()`), so the two walkers now disagree. Fix belongs on the new code path in editor.ts.

samples.summary: The new `listLevel` normalization exists only inside the planner; every other reader of `listLevel` still takes the raw collaborative value, so the invariant the new module documents is not enforced anywhere else
samples.evidence: `list-level.ts`'s `levelOf` (and its doc comment) justify itself by the fact that `listLevel` arrives unvalidated from a peer's Tree attribute. That read site is untouched: `packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:243` is still `block.listLevel = Number(attrs.listLevel)`, so `NaN` / `Infinity` / out-of-band values still enter the model. Every geometry and serialization consumer reads it raw and is unprotected by the planner: `packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:494` (`LIST_INDENT_PX * ((block.listLevel ?? 0) + 1)`), `view/layout.ts:1089`, `view/table-layout.ts:93`, `view/paint-layout.ts:198`, `view/peer-cursor.ts:392`, `view/table-renderer.ts:524`, `view/doc-canvas.ts:599`, `export/pdf-painter.ts:366`, `serialize/markdown.ts:140`. A poisoned level is therefore repaired only if a user happens to indent that exact block; until then the layout multiplies `NaN` into the marker/line geometry. Normalizing in `treeToDocument` (or in `levelOf`'s equivalent at the read seam) would make the guard total.

samples.summary: The two copies of `siblingsOf` disagree on how a stale parent map is tolerated: text-editor's throws where editor.ts's degrades
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1641` deliberately uses `doc.findBlock(cellInfo.tableBlockId)` with a comment that the parent map is only as fresh as the last layout pass, so a table removed since then must not "throw out of the middle of an indent gesture". The sibling implementation added in the same change, `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2893`, uses `this.doc.getBlock(info.tableBlockId)`, which throws `Block not found` on exactly that stale-map case — reached from `handleTab` / `handleIndent` / `handleOutdent`, i.e. out of a keystroke handler. Fix belongs on the new code (use `findBlock` there too).

samples.summary: `planListLevelChanges` silently depends on the `siblings` arrays being reference-stable across the whole walk, and nothing states or checks that precondition
samples.evidence: The grouping map is keyed by array identity (`new Map<ReadonlyArray<Block>, Set<string>>()` at packages/docs/src/model/list-level.ts:124, `groups.get(siblings)`). That holds today only because all three walkers read through `Doc`'s cached `_document` (`packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:158` returns `this._document.blocks` by reference) and no write happens during the walk. `YorkieDocStore.getDocument()` returns a fresh `cloneDocument(...)` on every call (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:629-652) and `Doc.setBlockType` calls `refresh()` after each write (document.ts:666), so a future walker that reads the store directly, or any caller that writes while walking, would hand a different array per block: each block becomes its own group, subtree carrying silently degrades to per-block moves, and no test would notice. Worth documenting the precondition on `planListLevelChanges` (or keying by a stable container id).

verdict.reason: The quoted strings exist, but they are not branch-authored reviewer-steering text and cannot be read as an authoritative verdict by any downstream reviewer. (1) `.agent-review/` is the review harness's own output directory for the current run: the panel is invoked with `--out .agent-review` (.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:896) and reads back `.agent-review/<lens>/summary.md` and `verdict.json` (lines 979, 996). The three subdirectories present (docs, design-fit, test-adequacy) are exactly the sibling lens ids reviewing this change, and `.agent-review/docs/stage-detail.json:1` holds orchestrator-computed `lensDiffSha256`/`lensFiles` metadata. `.agent-review/design-fit/summary.md:1` reports 2 minor and 2 nit findings with real file:line citations — a real lens verdict, not a planted blanket approval, so the characterization "pre-declared approvals" is not what the tree contains. (2) Independently, even if a branch did commit such a tree, both workflows delete it before any lens executes: `rm -rf .agent-review` at .github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:522-524 ("Clear stale verdicts") and .github/workflows/agent-review-on-demand.yml:253-254. The on-demand workflow explicitly documents this as the defense against exactly this attack at lines 452-453 ("cannot pick up a branch-planted `.agent-review/evil/stage-detail.json` because 'Clear stale verdicts' above does `rm -rf .agent-review`"). The stated harm — a later reviewer or agent reading these as an authoritative verdict — is therefore unreachable. Not gitignoring the path is inert given the pre-run wipe.

finding.summary: The new `levelOf` normalization protects only the planner; the layout pass still reads `listLevel` raw, where a non-finite value throws a RangeError and takes the whole layout down
finding.evidence: `list-level.ts` normalizes at "the single point of read" and its own comment concedes the layout "reads `listLevel` raw" — but the unprotected reader is worse than bad geometry. `packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:1091` does `levelCounters.length = Math.max(levelCounters.length, level + 1)` with `const level = block.listLevel ?? 0` (line 1089). With `level = NaN` that assignment is `arr.length = NaN` → `RangeError: Invalid array length` out of `computeLayout`; with a large finite level (> 2^32-1) the same. `layout.ts:494` also multiplies it into the indent. The value is reachable unvalidated: `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:495` does `block.listLevel = Number(attrs.listLevel)` on a peer's Tree attribute, and `packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:178` serializes whatever the content ingest supplies (`String(block.listLevel)`, no clamp, no schema bound anywhere in packages/backend/src). The diff's claim that a poisoned level is "repaired by the gesture that touches it" cannot hold here: layout runs on first render, before any gesture. Fix belongs on the raw readers (reuse the new `levelOf`/`MAX_LIST_LEVEL` in `layout.ts`), not on the planner.

verdict.reason: The absence claim checks out. levelOf (packages/docs/src/model/list-level.ts:29-33) is module-private — only MAX_LIST_LEVEL and planListLevelChanges are exported — so no other module can reuse it, and layout.ts contains no normalization at all (grep for isFinite/Math.floor/clamp in that file: zero matches). layout.ts:1089-1091 reads block.listLevel ?? 0 raw and assigns levelCounters.length = Math.max(len, level + 1), which throws RangeError: Invalid array length for NaN (ArraySetLength: ToUint32(NaN)=0 !== NaN) and for any finite level > 2^32-1; layout.ts:494 multiplies the same raw value into marginLeft. I searched for an upstream guard and found none: the only normalizing readers in the whole repo are clipboard.ts:348-351 (paste clamp) and list-level.ts:29-33, while both CRDT parse paths (model/crdt-tree.ts:243, frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:495) do a bare Number(attrs.listLevel) and the serializers do a bare String(block.listLevel) (yorkie-doc-store.ts:371, backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:178); there is no Yorkie schema or zod validation in packages/backend/src/yorkie. Every other reader is raw too (paint-layout.ts:198, doc-canvas.ts:599, table-layout.ts:93, table-renderer.ts:524, peer-cursor.ts:254,392, pdf-painter.ts:366,589). computeListCounters is a public export (index.ts:136) reached on first render (paint-layout.ts:133, doc-canvas.ts:242) and in PDF export (pdf-exporter.ts:124), so the "repaired by the gesture that touches it" rationale does not cover it. In lane: the new module asserts an invariant (finite level in [0, MAX_LIST_LEVEL]) that other consumers of the same field do not enforce, and the impact at the unguarded consumer is a thrown RangeError out of the layout pass. The one thing I could not exhibit is a concrete writer emitting a non-numeric or oversized attribute string; that affects likelihood, not the existence of the unguarded reader, and no boundary validation exists to rule it out.

mergedFrom.summary: `TextEditor.siblingsOf` resolves the parent table with throwing `getBlock`, where its `editor.ts` twin deliberately uses non-throwing `findBlock` for the same stale-map reason

finding.summary: New crash path: TextEditor.siblingsOf resolves the parent table with doc.getBlock (throws), unlike the editor.ts twin which deliberately uses findBlock
finding.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2890 `const tableBlock = this.doc.getBlock(info.tableBlockId);` — `getCellInfo` reads `getActiveLayout().blockParentMap`, which is only as fresh as the last layout pass. This file already treats that map as routinely stale: packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2971-2978 wraps arrow handling in try/catch with the comment "Stale blockParentMap data (e.g. table rows removed by remote edit)", and `Doc.getBlock` throws when the id no longer resolves (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:220-266 / findBlock returning undefined). `handleTab` (2699-2707), `handleIndent` (2762) and `handleOutdent` (2779) have no such guard, and before this change the cursor-only path never consulted the parent map at all — so a Tab/Cmd+] with the caret in a cell of a table deleted by a peer now throws out of the keydown handler mid-gesture. The diff's own editor.ts copy documents the opposite choice (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1632-1641, `findBlock`, "rather than throw out of the middle of an indent gesture"); the fix belongs on the new text-editor.ts code (use findBlock + optional chaining).

verdict.reason: The code is present as described: text-editor.ts:2893 resolves the parent table with the throwing `this.doc.getBlock(info.tableBlockId)` (Doc.getBlock throws at document.ts:215), while the twin helper editor.ts:1641 deliberately uses `doc.findBlock` with an explicit comment (editor.ts:1632-1634) that the map is only as fresh as the last layout pass and must not "throw out of the middle of an indent gesture". `getCellInfo` (text-editor.ts:3666-3671) reads `getActiveLayout().blockParentMap`, and `getLayout` is the injected `() => layout` closure (editor.ts:2525 over the `layout` variable at editor.ts:1108, refreshed only in recomputeLayout at 1511/1533), so it can lag the document — a staleness the file itself acknowledges twice (2974, 4634-4639 "never calls doc.getBlock ... must degrade ... rather than throw"). Reachable unguarded callers: handleIndent (2760) and handleOutdent (2777) via handleKeyDown case '[' / ']' (1306-1317); no try/catch covers them. The nearest guard, handleKeyDown:1026 (`!this.doc.findBlock(cursor.position.blockId)` → reset cursor and return), only ensures the caret block still exists; it does not exclude a surviving caret block whose stale map entry names a since-removed table, which is exactly the value dereferenced at 2893, so it does not make the path unreachable. One sub-claim is wrong — handleTab (2682) returns early through isInCell (3662-3664), which reads the same map, so Tab never reaches siblingsOf with cell info — but the Cmd+]/Cmd+[ path stands, leaving a real uncaught-throw-out-of-a-keystroke-handler defect.
